description: Hi! I’m Anusha, a final-year Computer Science student . I build in Python and web tech, and I’ve worked on projects like a WhatsApp chat analyzer and an accessibility tool for elderly web users. I’m excited about turning NASA’s abandoned Moon and Mars equipment into an interactive story. Looking for teammates with skills in frontend/UI design, storytelling or content writing, and animation or graphics. Let’s make space history come alive!
summary: Echoes of Space is an interactive digital space museum that tells the stories of the human-made objects left behind on the Moon and Mars. We built a working web app where visitors can explore a Moon and Mars map, browse a searchable archive of objects such as Surveyor 3, the Apollo 11 lunar module descent stage and the Apollo laser retroreflectors, and follow each mission from arrival to what was left behind. Every object has its own story, a source link and a confidence tag (confirmed, estimated or unknown), so facts are clearly separated from uncertainty. Learners can also take a discovery quiz, play mini games, earn badges and switch between Story Mode for young explorers and Explorer Mode for full detail. The project uses NASA open data, including the NASA Image and Video Library, NASA Trek, LROC imagery and NSSDCA mission records. It matters because these objects are part of humanity's space heritage, and they raise real questions about preservation, planetary protection and responsible exploration.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

Echoes of Space is an interactive digital space museum about the objects humanity has left on the Moon and Mars. Visitors can:

- Explore a Moon and Mars map. Switch between the two worlds, zoom, and tap a marker to open an object, or use the "Fly To" buttons to jump to landing sites.

- Browse a searchable archive of objects such as Surveyor 3, the Apollo 11 lunar module descent stage and the Apollo laser retroreflectors. Filter by world, category and status, and sort by year.

- Follow the Mission Timeline for each mission, from arrival to what was left behind.

- Read each object's story, with its mission, purpose, why it was left behind and why it matters today.

- Learn in the Archaeology Lab, then take a 10-question quiz and mini games (Match Game, Spot the Site) and earn badges.

- Switch between Story Mode for young explorers and Explorer Mode for full detail.

HOW IT USES NASA DATA

Object records, mission facts, dates, coordinates and images come from NASA sources: the NASA Image and Video Library, NASA Trek, LROC imagery and NSSDCA mission records. Every object carries a source link and a confidence tag (CONFIRMED, ESTIMATED or UNKNOWN), so visitors can see what is documented and what is uncertain. Our Sources page lists every object with its tag and NASA reference.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

- Makes space history approachable and playful for children, families and students.

- Raises awareness of space heritage, planetary protection and the question of whether to preserve or retrieve abandoned equipment.

- Shows how NASA's open data can be turned into learning experiences.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

[Edit to match your build] React with Vite and Tailwind CSS for the front end, Flask (Python) for the API, SQLite for the database, and Leaflet for the interactive map.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

Instead of a plain database, each object is treated like an archaeological find with its own story. A mascot guide, a mission "lifecycle" (arrived, worked, left behind), badges and games make learning feel like an adventure, while confidence tags keep the science honest.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Accuracy first: we avoided unverified claims and labelled uncertainty.

- Accessibility and audience: two reading modes for different ages, readable contrast, and a responsive layout.

- Credit and licensing: NASA imagery is credited to NASA. This is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA.

- Future scope: more missions and sites, a classroom mode, and an AI Space Archivist that answers only from verified project data.
